designSummary: Single-group prospective follow-up with outcomes at entry, 6 and 12 months; descriptive estimation with confidence intervals, no hypothesis test against a comparator.
sampleSize: About 85 participants in 12 months (88 entered in the pathway's first year). With a standard deviation of about 30 percentage points for percent change in dose (two-clinic follow-up), 85 participants give a 95 percent confidence interval of about 6.4 percentage points either side of the mean. For the descriptive proportion reaching a 25 percent reduction, an expected 40 percent gives an interval of about 10 percentage points either side. About 20 disengagement events are expected, which supports a model with at most two predictors.
primaryAnalysis: Mean percent change in daily dose at 6 months with a 95 percent confidence interval, using dispensing data for everyone who consented, including participants who left the pathway.
secondaryAnalysis: Mixed model of pain interference at entry, 6 and 12 months; description of withdrawal checklist scores around dose steps; counts and rates of emergency visits and overdose; logistic regression of disengagement on distance over 60 km and interpreter need.
missingData: Dose is missing only when dispensing data are absent; those participants are reported and handled by multiple imputation in a sensitivity analysis. Missing pain interference is not imputed in the primary description; a sensitivity analysis compares completers with all participants.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes are described with intervals and are not tested.
software: R with standard packages for mixed models and multiple imputation; code kept with the analysis plan.
overfittingGuards: Two predictors only in the disengagement model
Analysis plan fixed before data collection
No subgroup testing beyond distance and interpreter need
summary: Descriptive estimates with intervals from about 85 participants; the disengagement model is limited to two predictors.
